records.claim: There have been a few reports of erectile dysfunction (trouble getting or keeping an erection) and ejaculatory problems (no semen released) in men taking isotretinoin. Changes in sperm morphology (size and shape) have also been reported. This could affect men’s fertility (ability to make healthy sperm). Studies have not been done in men to see if isotretinoin could increase the chance of birth defects. In general, exposures that fathers or sperm donors have are unlikely to increase risks to a pregnancy. For more information, please see the MotherToBaby fact sheet Paternal Exposures at https://mothertobaby.org/fact-sheets/paternal-exposures-pregnancy/.
records.source_section: If a man takes isotretinoin, could it affect fertility or increase the chance of birth defects?
